Hornets make honey?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Better than wasp honey, not as good as bee.
We finally have a man on the inside. We're gonna put Bart Simpson away for a long, long time.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: By law, the most we can give him is a ten day suspension.
Skinner! Your bus driver just totaled my Camry!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Can I offer you the use of my Merkur?
Wake up! You're on!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Children, I have some exciting news.
In recognition of your twenty years as Interim Principal, I hereby dedicate the Seymour Skinner Parking Annex.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Did they have to guess the date of my death?
Skinner! You've got to deal with these kooks!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Don't worry, I have a plan: pretend I agree with them.
WOULD SHE SHUT HER TRAP...

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: FOR A GIFT CARD FROM THE GAP?
Skinner! People want to get home! Speak regular!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Fine, we'll start the raffle and skip the things no one wants, like art projects by your children.
They're all the same, Gloomhilda.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: First Place goes to Bart Simpson and Martin Prince...
Skin-ner! That song needed no lyrical improvement.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Gary... Gary, you know what you need?
Let's sing while we think. It'll make it more fun for everyone.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: HOW DO WE GAG A BLAB-BERMOUTH LIKE LISA?
HOW DO WE CRUSH HER FIRST AMENDMENT RIGHTS?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: HOW DO WE STOP HER WRITING UP WHAT SHE SAW?
According to this file from Blazing Guy Secret Security, your behavior was so egregious we can do something that we've never done before: fire a teacher.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Hand in your red pen.
I know you're there, Skinner! I'd recognize those discolored Hush Puppies anywhere.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Hear that? He thinks my Try 'N' Save brand Shush Mutts are genuine Hush Puppies.
Uh, what's that say under your hand there?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Hm, it's an unrelated article.
Welcome, everyone, to the annual Donkey Basketball Classic. I'm sure that mule enjoy it.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Hm, tough crowd. Uh, would everyone just rise for our National Anthem?
Two R's come October.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Hm. What do you think of the banners?
Consider it done.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: How about you, Bart? Let me guess, you forgot to bring something.
Well, you should've.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: How could I? She wasn't even born yet.
So long, "superstars.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I can't believe it. Superintendent Chalmers betrayed me. After all the wrapping paper I bought from his daughter.
When I say "drive us to Bolivia," that is your cue to start the damn car!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I can't find the key!
Ow!Ow!Ow!Ow! Skinner!!! Why aren't these uniforms colorfast?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I don't understand it. I got them at the same place I buy Mother's dresses. Good Lord! Mother's in the park!
Oh, oh, so you also heard about the eleven dollars an hour.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I heard about it first.
Excuse me, I don't belong here -- I am not bald! I am balding! Why will no one honor the ding?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I honor the ding, sir.
Skinner! How are we going to raise school spirit with this sappy hokum?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I know, sir. It's an embarrassment.
I'm sorry, what did you say?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I said, I'm lop-shouldered! And I have been since I was hung by my armpits in a North Vietnamese prison!
He's got your key, Seymour.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I suppose you want to know why this all happened. Picture what I'm describing in your minds.
Yes, if I recall, you took a sick day you did not have.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I was gonna lose my foot.
Nothing can ameliorate the ineptitude of Principal Skinner.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I wish he wouldn't use me in every example.
And now, the climactic Race Around the School. Previous winners include Sideshow Mel, Señora Bumblebee Man...and Olympian Edwin Moses.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I'll bet your biggest hurdle was leaving your beloved hometown.
I'd say you're dumb as a post. But at least you can put a sign on a post that says "fresh strawberries -- one mile." You are a nitwit in an ill-fitting suit.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I'll have you know I'm lop-shouldered.
You know, I used to think a car was just a way of getting from Point A to Point B... and on weekends, Point C. But that was the old me. That man died the moment I laid eyes on the 1979 Honda Accord.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I've always admired car owners. And I hope to be one myself, as soon as I finish paying off Mother. She insists I pay her retroactively for the food I ate as a child.
And of course, Springfield Elementary is closed. We were just messing with Bart Simpson.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I've got one! Springfield El...bow Macaroni Factory.
Hm, it sounded like battle.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I've had a cold.
And a pill popper.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: If I could just...
Yes, except for one small glitch. We could only afford to rent the mannequins.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: If we didn't get them back by five, we'd be charged for the extra day.
There's no need for hyperbole, Seymour.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: If you think it's so easy to handle Bart Simpson, why don't you do it yourself?!
What kind of man wears Armour Hot Dogs?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: It was a good idea, Bart. But it's just not working.
That's not so bad.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: It's a little bad!
Well Seymour, I certainly appreciate you letting me store my collection of antique cologne bottles in your office while they re-carpet my condo.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: It's quite a collection, and I assume, irreplaceable.
Seymour, those string beans were cooked to perfection. After twenty years I am finally starting to like you.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Just wait for dessert, sir. I made it with you in mind.
No one goes near that boy till the ambulance comes! Any physical contact violates our school's no-touch policy.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Let's quickly prod him to the curb with this pool skimmer.
That's why it was shut down and moved here brick by brick.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Look around, Lisa. That grant money could do a lot of good.
You'll be happy, they'll be happy, and I can go home and enjoy some delicious fondue.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Made with the fondue set I bought you for Christmas?
Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Mother doesn't approve of me dating, so I need you to keep her busy for a few hours while Edna and I sneak out.
Thank you, Willie. Now please return it to its plastic snap case.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Moving on, our class trip to Italy is now spaghetti night at Papa John's, and your fifteen-hundred dollar deposits will not be refunded.
Did that boy say what's a battle?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: No he said what's that rattle. It's about the heating duct.
You mean this boy, here?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: No! No! Lisa Simpson!
Skinner!! Get off of my school!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: No! You get off of my school!
Did you wear those same clothes yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: No, I have two identical sets of these clothes.
I thought we were having steamed clams.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: No, no. I said "steamed hams." That's what I call hamburgers.
Well you better hurry. Look what they've done to your car.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: No, that's how it always looks.
Ow, ow, ow. Seymour I was thinking of promoting you to Assistant Superintendent. But, instead, that plum goes to Holloway.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: No. But sir, he's a drunk.
Will someone remove that crazy man, please?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: No...No he's, he's not crazy. It's true: I'm, I'm an impostor. That man is the real Seymour Skinner.
Ooh, I have had it. I have had it with this school, Skinner: the low test scores, class after class of ugly, ugly children...

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Now, really I hardly think the children's appearance should --
Well, we could give each student a full college scholarship.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Oh mercy. Seriously though, before we draw up the budget, I believe the students and faculty have a few suggestions...
I... I didn't know that.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Oh the list of things you don't know could fill a week's worth of morning announcements, with enough left over for a send-home flyer!
T-shirt? Why don't you just give me a sandwich board that says "Male Prostitute"?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Oh well... I... Forgive me, sir.
Really. Well, I'm from Utica and I've never heard anyone use the phrase "steamed hams.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Oh, not in Utica, no. It's an Albany expression.
No, I said you were fired.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Oh. That's much worse.
Nothing. I just bought myself a car!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Oh... oh, good. This will sound crazy but at first I... I thought I'd enraged you again.
You were supposed to call as soon as the new scoreboard was in. Tell me, does it play that song "Charge"?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Ohhh, does it ever!
We could try it out this weekend at the "Faculty Follies" after-party.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: One thing -- what if there's a woman we both like?
I feel for you, Seymour. If you ever need a shoulder to lean on, I'm here for you.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: P.S., Chalmers and I are doing it.
I hear you've been encouraging a student's creativity!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Please sir, I can explain...
The second that boy fails, we're knocking down this school.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Please, have a little faith.
By the time you finish talking, we're gonna be opening this damn capsule.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Right. Time capsule. Nelson. Give me something.
Ah, if it isn't Eavesdrop Ernie and the Listen-In Bunch! I'd like you boys to meet Dahlia Brinkley.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: She's the only Springfield Elementary alum ever to advance to the Ivy League!
Uh-huh. Skinner, what is going on here?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Sir, if we let these hill folk into our school, our test scores would drop so low, we'd lose all federal funding.
My 'H' has been stolen! Oh! That's how people know it's a Honda! What's the point of having a Honda if you can't show it off?!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Sir, if you'll just stop yelling at me, I'm sure I can find a replacement...
Skinner, be gay on your own time. Today's the day we choose who gets the school's vending-machine contract! I anticipate quite the dog and pony show.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Sir, this school has a strict no-animal policy. I assume these are hypothetical dogs and poni?
Skinner!!! Why are there children walking on my head?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: So we meet again, Mad Magazine...
Hello, Seymour.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: So what's the word down at One School Board Plaza?
So does a leaf blower. Look, the district can't afford to keep every school open. So all the kids will take a standardized test, and whichever school scores the lowest will be closed forever.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: So you're saying if our kids don't pass this test, you're shutting down Springfield Elementary?
The answer is simple, Seymour. Get a corporate sponsor. But don't worry, you won't have to compromise yourself.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: So, from now on our cafeteria will only serve... delicious "Stuffwich's" heroes, hoagies, and torpedoes.
What do you think?!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: So, how did we do?
Seymour, as superintendent I supervise every school in the district.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: So... you're over-seeing other people?
Banff, shmanff! I'm talking about Sundance!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Sundance, the preeminent independent film festival held each January in Park City Utah?
Skinner!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Superintendent Chalmers, you didn't have to come all the way down here. Everything's under control.
Sey-mour!!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Superintendent! I was just... eh... stretching my calves on the windowsill! Isometric exercise. Care to join me?
Skinner, I was a little wary of bringing these veterans of Iwo Jima to tour your school, but I see my fears were unfounded.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Thank you, sir. And what more fitting finale than to gaze reverently at Old Glory.
Skin-ner! Just let him kill you already.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: That's the man I was telling you about.
It's on page one of the rule book!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: That's where I doodle.
Can't you say anything in a normal way?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: The answer, sadly, is not yes.
Skinner!! I'm worried. This girl is extremely popular and thinks for herself. She's like a female Eleanor Roosevelt.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: The students will do anything she says. She's captured their imagination like a bright piece of construction paper.
Yes, yes, I-I knew that.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: There's no hope for you, Simpson. You'll be locked in detention until you graduate to the penal system.
Don't bother screaming for help... this is a municipal, off-cycle election.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: There's no one for miles.
Is that a grown man going between the children's legs?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: There's nothing in the rule book against it.
You were asked to chug-a-lug. And a-lug you shall chug!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: There's something I've wanted to say to you for a long time. Am I a good principal?
Way to make a deal, Seymour!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: They don't even know that my pockets are full of bottled water and cornbread!

Edna, until the state disciplinary committee rules on your case, every workday you'll report to a school board holding facility -- an educational limbo as it were, where you are the un-baptized dead baby.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: They never seem to like that analogy.
Nothing but transparent toadying.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: They were the children's idea. I tried to stop them.
I see, with a stain on the shirt in the exact same place?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Things aren't good at home.
Dear God have mercy... Seymour... your new teacher is... everybody pray!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: This is a public school!
Skinner?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Today I received an education in how children really learn: by seeing their principal run around on top of a shipping container.
Huh, how sad.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Today we celebrate the first of many, many, many, many diversity forums.
Uh-huh. What region?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Uh, Upstate New York.
I-- Oh. Well, I was born in Queens, went to Ball State, then made the move to Intercourse, Pennsylvania. Eh, why do you ask?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Uh, don't worry, sir, I'll teach these children some respect for their town. I'm assigning each of you twenty hours of community service.

The whole town's in an uproar about your sleazy shenanigans! Now I'm going to give you a choice. You can give up this tawdry, fulfilling relationship, or you two will be out of here so fast your mortarboards will spin. And where is your mortarboard, anyway?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Uh, right here, sir!
What are you doing in that ridiculous duffel, Seymour? And is that burning literature I smell?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Uh, well sir, I uh...
Skinner! What factory makes just one kind of pasta?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Uh, well, I just thought, uh... specialization being the wave of the future... uh, probably...
Finding out about what, Seymour?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Um... about how early press coverage of the bake sale is uniformly positive.
I won't be happy to hear what, Seymour?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Um... that uh... bake sale revenue projections are through the roof.
We're dropping the geography requirement. The children weren't testing well. It was proving to be an embarrassment.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Very good. Back to the three R's.
I'd fire that man if he weren't so damn good at what he does.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: We have a school full of professionals, sir.
You said you were getting rid of that nest.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: We trade the honey for chalk and yardsticks.
You have got to end this thing, Seymour.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: We're not coming down until our jobs are reinstated and you acknowledge and celebrate our love.
Forty-eight... forty-nine... fifty. Flag's up to date. Very good, Seymour. Now, are these children as smart as they look?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well let's pick one at random. How about that one?
Seymour, you are truly incompetent.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, I hardly think it's fair to...
Yes, all of them. Why Seymour, it seems I left my sunglasses on the bus.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, I'd best retrieve them.
I have seven other principals and I've never yelled their names, not even once! You know what these kids lack?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, certainly not a caring superintendent.
Yeah. Nice to see you. Seymour, why is that student lying unconscious on the floor?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, in many cases the floor is the best... oh look! Here comes Lumpy, the school snake!

Well, I've gotta hand it to you, Seymour. These drab student coverings have created the perfect distraction-free environment, thus preparing the children for permanent positions in tomorrow's mills and processing facilities. Best of all, with less than a minute to go before I leave, absolutely nothing has gone wrong.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, it is starting to rain, but I can hardly be blamed for that, can I?
Skin-ner!! How could you put this boy on with that horrible material?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, it really did seem funny in rehearsal.
So what's your story, Seymour? If that is your real name.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, obviously it isn't. My real name is Armin Tamzarian.
Sexless freak.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, seems as though we're just about at the halfway point, so why don't we call it intermission?
Yeah, all right. Just come on down.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, this is it.
The whole school is made up of modeling clay -- every afternoon they reshape it, just to get my goat.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, with some school band music and added effects, we could show Lisa's film at the public library.
Seymour, you run a tight ship.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, you know what they say, sir. "Where there's no smoke, there's no fire.
So what'll it be, Seymour?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well... I'm sorry, but, ah, I can't give up the woman I love.
Skinner!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: What I wouldn't give for something to interrupt this awkward moment.
I'm sorry if you misunderstood our arrangement.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: What am I supposed to tell our children?
Well, we'll use the time-honored "I saw her first" rule.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: What if I see her hand at the same time you see her face?
Can't you be a team player just once?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: When I was starting out, they said "You're good -- but are you 'plaque' good?" Well, today I can say "Yes I am!
Skinner! We have got to get these kids back in school.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Willie, can't you turn your hose on them?
Yes. And you call them steamed hams despite the fact they are obviously grilled?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Y... you know... one thing I sho... Excuse me for one second.
Do you know what today is?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Yes! Of course I do. HAPPY BIRTHDAY TO YOU / HA--
Skin-ner! This dessert menu is funnier than you!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Yes, but I'm funnier than the cocktail napkins.
They're blank, Seymour.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Yes, but there're two k-sounds in "cocktail.
It's always the children's fault, isn't it, Seymour?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Yes, yes it is, sir.
You call hamburgers "steamed hams?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Yes. It's a regional dialect.
Well, Seymour, it seems we've put together a baseball team, and I was wondering -- who's on first?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Yes. Not the pronoun, but rather a player with the unlikely name of "Who" is on first.
It's an unrelated article. Within the banner headline?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Yes. Now, to re-direct our conversation slightly, I had a few ideas on how to spend this oil money.
Wait! Wait! There's no need to leave!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: You showed up before the students! That's all we asked!
Skinner! I don't mean to interrupt your advice from the janitor. But I say, cut off the head and the body will die.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: You want to get rid of Lisa?! But she's such a good student!
I don't want to have to yell at you.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: You yell at me about everything.
Well, I'm not made of stone.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: You're not made of stone... a brick and you're... made of stone...

Right here, ma'am. Oh boy, a "put back!" I hope it takes me by the freezer section. Stick my head in the pizza case it's like a ski vacation! I can imagine the pepperonis are Swiss chalets nestled in a big layer of mozzarella snow!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Bart, eyewitnesses to your fight described you as "berserkoid," "totally aggro," and said you punched Milhouse "like fifty billion times." That's an excessive number of times.
Ah, she's a beaut. You can't beat a Coleco. How many can I put you down for? A lot? Please say a lot. I need this.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I don't know. I'm not even sure we can keep this one. It's up to Lisa.
Tell this dummy mother exactly how you feel, right now.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I'm annoyed with you, Mother. Not just annoyed... Angry! I'm a grown man now! And I can run MY OWN LIFE!!
Shh. Shh. Calm down. Calm down. Aw, moving. You can sit down now...

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: We're still going antiquing on Saturday, right, mother?
Not yet. Let's get some lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, children, any questions for Postmaster Bill?
Venezuela, here I come!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: ... and while the school's only ball is being repaired...
I won't tell if you put me on the guest list.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: All right. Plus one?

I have reconstructed the ultimate instrument of colonial justice: the dunking stool. If the alleged witches survive the dunking, they clearly were witches. If they drown, then they were clearly innocent.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: And after this, it will be featured in the fifth-grade play "The Crucible"!
All right.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: And when you're done, here are the keys to your new shack.
Save your strength, lad. There's a whole field for to resod yet.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Bart, you wouldn't happen to know what sort of candy your Aunt Patty likes, would you?
Enjoy your flight!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Brilliant plan to remove all the underperformers for test day, sir.
Looks like the falconry club's back from the dead!

dialogue.text: Ah Mother, may I read a magazine while I wait in the car?
It's okay, Marge. I've learned my lesson. A mountain of sugar is too much for one man. It's clear now why God portions it out in those tiny packets and why he lives on a plantation in Hawaii.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Ah, Diorama-rama. My favorite school event next to Hearing Test Thursday.
Uh, Marge? I don't want to ruin the moment, but you got something stuck between your-- ohhh...

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Ah, a peaceful Saturday afternoon, with no Bart Simpson -- and no Milhouse, for that matter. Nothing on my agenda but to sit here and watch hummingbirds.
Lower!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Ah, this is as romantic as the night I proposed.
Hey, what's this thing?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Ah, yes. Uh, take a good look at him, Nelson, cause that's where you're headed.
I'm not stealing it. Hotels expect you to take a few things. It's a souvenir.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Ah. Is that my necktie you're wearing?
Welcome aboard. It wasn't any easier.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Ahhh, these uniforms are a godsend. Horseplay is down 40 percent. Youthful exuberance has been cut in half, and high spirits are at an all-time low.
Twister! Get down!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Air Skinner" brings it up. He bounces the ball repeatedly, in a dribbling-type motion.
Wait a minute... I knew you were a neat freak, Skinner. But you beat your rug till it bleeds?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: All right, I'll come clean. I woke up and, surprisingly, mother wasn't there beside me. She was dead.
To alcohol! The cause of, and solution to, all of life's problems!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: And finally, the bake sale to raise money for the car wash has been canceled, due to confusion. Well, that concludes this morning's announcements. I'm Seymour Skinner and stand by to resume learning in five, four, three, two, one...
Oh, there are pictures. I keep them where I need the most cheering up.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: And now, to top off our most propane-explosion-free Science Week ever, our grand finale! The launching of a weather balloon.
Aw, that's Tooth Fairy money down the drain, sweetie. I never win anything. It's always some stupid jerk you've never heard of.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: And the winner is...
Well, I want that one.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: And the winner of the blimp ride is... Homer Simpson!
Hey, you can't fool us. We're from the "Learn to Fart" state.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Bart and Lisa are lost in Capital City and presumed crying.
Show you what it's like in the real world!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Bart, because of your sister's restraining order, there is no place in this school you can legally occupy, without violating your order. Observe.
Baby, I hope you've got snuggle insurance, 'cause I'm about to file a claim.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Bart, do you have your slingshot?
Wait a minute...

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Bart, we need to talk to you about your practice test.
Ya know, I think you're right. First thing tomorrow morning, I'm gonna punch Lenny in the back of the head.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Batten down those cowlicks... straighten that part... uncross those eyes, Mister.
Ow! Ow! He bit me! You saw him! He bit me! You little...

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Before we begin, children, may I remind you the school computers are not to be used to access PrincipalSkinnerStinks.com, Skinnersucks.org or Shavedskinner.edu.
Ho-mer, Ho-mer, Ho-mer..

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: But first, our second-prize winner, and the recipient of this handsome shoe buffer... Ned Flanders!
Yeah, he's somethin' else, all right.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: But worst of all, he drags down the grades of anyone who sits near him. Just look at this pattern.
Oh.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: By itself something like this might not call for an extreme penalty...but this is not an isolated incident. Bart's behavior is unruly. He's frequently absent from school, then gives teachers pathetic excuse notes...that are obviously childish forgeries when compared to...
I 'unno... Internet?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Children, it seems the phone lines are down. So I'm afraid we're stuck here for the duration.
Rockin

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Children, you're in for a treat. Today's assembly is devoted to a special kind of history.
I thought I heard clicks and pops!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Children, your test scores are down because we've been having so many assemblies, you haven't had time to study. This assembly will remedy that.
So long, suckers!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Damn! They're very slowly getting away.
Don't buy it! I bought one last year and it was crap construction!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Do I hear fifty dollars?
Lisa, the world is a very complicated place. And when you get right down to it... cannonball!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Do you think there's a place in the hip-hop world for a forty-something elementary school administrator?
Remember to rebel against authority, kids.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Don't listen to him, children.
Sugar Man!!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Door to door sugar? What a marvelous idea! What's that, mother? I'm just talking to the sugar man. Mother, I'm a big boy. I can do as I wish. Excuse me.
Okay, just repeat after me. "Edna, I made a huge mistake and I want you back.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Edna, I made a huge mistake and I want you back. How's that, Homer?
Dressing room? Uh oh.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Edna, we don't need wedding china. The dishes mother won on "Let's Make A Deal" are holding up nicely.
We're going to build the world's tallest human pyramid!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Finally, this town will have a real claim to fame.
Oh, I've only got a hundred dollars. I'd better bid shrewdly.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: First up is this video camera.
Eww, lemon... ugh, cherry... hmm, custard... mmm, purple.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: For the next week I stayed alive by eating my mother's delicious preserves and maintained my sanity by dribbling a nearby basketball with my one free hand. I made a game of it, seeing how many times I could bounce the ball in a day, then trying to break that record. Occasionally the police arrived to search my home.

Look at it this way: you're a free man... unlike me. You have all your hair... unlike me. No kids tying you down, or a crippling mortgage that you refinanced at twenty-six percent because a dancing internet cowboy told you to... Oh, God, I hate my life!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Gee. Compared to you, my life is one big half-day!
Dick Fiddler!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Gentlemen, I can't run away from what I've done. I accept that I killed my mother. My whole life she's belittled me! Maybe deep down... I'm glad.
Then came the day we knew we were finished.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Gentlemen, US Magazine just came out with its "What's Hot and What's Not Issue.
Boy, a good man really is hard to find.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Gentlemen, according to my sources you are planning to simultaneously drop your pencils at 2:15 this afternoon. Do so and you will be suspended.
New Springfield rocks!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Go ahead and laugh! We have a better town bird!
Will you two shut up?! People are trying to sleep!!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Great Barrier Reef! We're under attack!
Marge, look at all this great stuff I found at the marina! It was just sitting in some guy's boat!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Hello, Simpson. I'm riding the bus today because Mother hid my car keys to punish me for talking to a woman on the phone. She was right to do it.
Paddles down! It's the only way to change the system!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Hello? Calling from England? Certainly I can put you on speakerphone.
Woo hoo!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Hm. Fifteen years of loyal service and this is how they tell me -- a jester with an invisible proclamation.
That is so true.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Hmmm. These campaign buttons are all partisan. Don't you have any neutral ones? "May The Better Man Win?"... "Let's Have a Good, Clean Election?" That sort of thing?
What are you trying to tell me, Skinner?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Homer, Lenny...my man... I could never lie to you guys. I'm starting to get cold feet. Please don't tell anyone.
Marge, guess what! Skinner wants to bail on his wedding!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Homer, you're still talking to me!
Man cave! Everyone's welcome to my man cave!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I assure you, we've spared no effort to accommodate your special-needs student.
Hey Skinner! Do you and Edna want to join Marge and me at "Great Moments With Mr. Eisner"?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I believe the only venue for me is the ride of broken dreams.
There are perfectly good answers to those questions, but they'll have to wait for another night. Now off to bed.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I can't remember the last time we were all together.
What have you done this time, boy?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I caught your son defacing school property this morning. We estimate the damage at seventy-five dollars and, frankly, we think it's terribly unfair that other taxpayers should foot the bill.
I thought he was dead.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I suppose you're all wondering where I've been. It all started a week ago. I was at my desk, revising and updating the school dress codes, when...
Oh, thank God there's a fire. Marge's birthday's comin' up.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I think what she would treasure most is a gift bought through honest effort. Because...
The deed is done.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I wish you'd asked me before you...
On my chess set, the pawns are all Hamburglars.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I'M SO HAPPY WITH MY EVIL PLAN / SAY GOODBYE TO MUSIC, GYM AND ART / SOON WE WILL HAVE THE PERFECT SCHOOL / WHERE FUN AND EXCITEMENT NEVER START!
Thank you for getting me out of work.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I'll be blunt. Bart's latest escapade goes far beyond the realm of the hijink.
Does it still keep hot drinks hot and cold drinks cold?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I'm afraid it doesn't keep any drinks anything.
What is it this time?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I'm afraid this time the victims are the innocent blades of grass on Groundskeeper Willie's award-winning play field. If it's all right with you, Bart will repay his debt to society through back-breaking physical labor, re-sodding the field manually, seed by seed.
Yeah, but what about Bart?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I'm sure he'll pick up enough to get by. And the whole thing won't cost you a dime as long you're willing to take in a student of your own.
What do you mean? And who are you?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: I'm your son's principal, and the Washington Monument is the most uninspired model choice there is. It's like saying "I don't care. My kid's a loser.
Oh, I know! But how can I undo eight years of jerkiness in two easy sessions at no cost to me?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: If I may make a suggestion.
What does sequestered mean?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: If the jury is deadlocked, they're put up in a hotel together so they can't communicate with the outside world.
Well if you change your mind it'll be in my freezer. But only for a week. Got a lot of ice cream comin' in.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: If this were a movie mother wouldn't let me watch it.
What does deadlocked mean?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: It's when the jury can't agree on a verdict.
Whoo-hoo!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Just think what we can buy with that money. History books that know how the Korean War came out. Math books that don't have that Base six crap in them.
Shut up! I didn't tell you to say that!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Just why am I taking your advice?
Where we'll get... a free room, free food, free swimming pool, free HBO - Oooh, "Free Willy!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Justice is not a frivolous thing, Simpson. It has little, if anything, to do with a disobedient whale. Now let's vote.
Yeah!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Ladies and gentlemen, the unthinkable has happened. Some sick, twisted individual has stolen every teacher's edition in this school.
Have a good time! Wait a minute.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Lisa, I know I can trust you to inventory this Glee Club peanut brittle.
Marge, it happened again!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Lisa? Lisa Simpson? You have ten seconds to get to the podium!
Why can't you support my gibberish? I'd do it if you were stupid!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Marge, Homer, this marital discord is perfect. But please, save it for home where your son could see it.
All right then.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Martin Prince, report to my office at once!
Marge, this is perfect for both of us! It's got bowling for me and sweeping for you!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Maybe you'd like to give it a try?
Oh, hello Principal Skinner. I'd get up but the boy crippled me.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Mmm-hmm. I understand completely. The disturbing incident I was referring to happened this morning, when your son flushed an explosive device down the boys' lavatory.
Woo-Hoo!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Mother, get an extra-special hug ready. I've bought you a new juicer!
Have fun at school, kids.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Mr. Simpson, this zone is for school buses only.
Hey, Skinner! Wanna drag race?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: My high school sweetheart was killed in a drag racing accident.
Look, you kill them, I get rid of them. That's always been our deal. But I do have one question: do you want the head?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: No! No! God no!
You mean all white with pink eyes?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: No, no, no, no. A student from Albania. It's a country on the Adriatic Sea.
I have a Boyle on my ass.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Now Willie, don't tell anyone I'm trying my stand-up comedy act tonight. If the students find out I'm performing at Floppy's, I'll never live it down.
I'm down.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Now, be careful with those video cameras, children. In order to buy them, the school board had to eliminate geography.
If anyone wants me, I'll be eating alone in the basement.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Now, uh, people, there's been some confusion about our bird-sighting rules. You cannot count birds that you've seen at the zoo, on stamps, or in dreams.
Where are the refreshments?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Now, you keep asking me that. And I keep telling you, over there.

Okay guys, I've got a secret play I've been saving for the Olympics or possibly the Final Four, and it goes something like this... Uh, Skinner I want you... Moe, you can take... Homer, you can take Groundskeeper Willie. No way am I taking Groundskeeper Willie. Yes you are. Are you a team player or not?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Oh my goodness, an untied shoelace. I'll just get down on one knee and retie that.
Like what?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Oh noW, we're into the dregs. Here's Ralph Wiggum's entry.
I pity the fool who doesn't like... he. And wher's Barney?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Oh, he's with his new girlfriend. The Japanese conceptual artist.
Telemarketing, eh?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Oh, you think this stolen 'H' is a laugh riot, don't you? Well, I'll tell you something that's not so funny: right now, Superintendent Chalmers is at home crying like a little girl!
I can't make it in today, Mr. Smithers. I have Smallpox... Well, it wasn't wiped out in my house.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Okay, delegates. You leave tomorrow for the statewide model U.N., so this is our last chance to bone up. And bone we will.
But enough about Bart. Tell me, Principal Skinner, are you married?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Only to my job.
Thanks, Marge.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Out of gas! But how?! I put a dollar in this morning and we've only driven ninety cents.
Marge, you're a genius.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: People let's have good assembly manners. People, people. Quiet down, now, please. Don't make me flick the lights on and off. Thank you. Ladies, gentlemen, parents and music lovers. Welcome to the first in a series of Saturday evening concerts.
What? Time to go?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Please, Mr. Simpson. I'm afraid I'll have to expel your son.
Really? Boy, it sucks to be you. Anyhoo, if there's one thing I know, it's how to win back a furious woman. We'll go to her house, and I'll whisper to you exactly what to say.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Really? You'll be my Cyrano?
Sorry, Maggie.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Say Simpson, would you mind holding one end of this banner while I put it up?
Sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Say what they will about our cafeteria, I-I still think they're the best Tater Tots money can buy.
No, this is about you. Edna wants to break up.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: She wants to break up?
Woo-hoo! Business trip!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Simpson! I'll teach you to make a Poupon "me!
Come i-in!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: So Bart, our school policy is to give students in your situation straight A's.
Seymour... Edna asked me to talk to you.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Splendid! Shall we discuss music, or the weather?
Woo hoo!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Students, each one of you has been assigned the mandatory honor of contributing to the Springfield Time Capsule...where your arcana will lie dormant until the thirty-first century...and...
Oh, me and my trenchant mouth.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Terrible, just terrible. You know, they seem to get worse every year.
Exactly. You're good looking, have a decent job... what lonely widow wouldn't consider you an option?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Thanks, Homer. I don't think the school pep squad could've cheered me up more. And they were state runners up in nineteen ninety-seven!
Wait a minute. I thought you didn't wanna get married.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: That was before I missed her smell, her warmth, her beautiful, beautiful penmanship!
My wife thinks you want me to pay for it.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: That was the idea.
...so, killing people together has really spiced things up in the bedroom.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: That's terrific, but I called you here to discuss your son's misbehavior on the school bus.
To the little girl's room!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: That's the collection money!
Come on! It'll be fun!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: That's what Debbie Sue said...
Mm-hmm!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: The 2nd Battle of Springfield was fought by the North...the South...and the East...to keep Springfield in, out of, and next to the Union, respectively. Now, the actual battle was fought over there, where that man is standing. But he won't move, so we'll do it here.
Oh, it's Lisa. That's ours.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: The fourth grade will now favor us with a melody, medley of holiday flavorites.
Lotta people at the dump today.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Their leader seems to be a woman.
Rye am Romer Rimpson...

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: There is only one class left, but it happens to be the "coolest" one of all.
Because I'm successfully married.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: There's no ring on that finger.
A little!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: These are Bart's uncompleted homework assignments for the last month: worksheets, problem sets, book reports, math jumbles, dioramas, topic sentences, conclusions, bibliographies, synonyms, mean-the-sames, define-a-likes, word twins and one Thanksgiving hand-turkey.
Yeah, we're awesome. This'll make a great toilet seat!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Uh, gentlemen... I'm uh... I'm starting to wonder if we've crossed a line here.
I hope it's Flanders. I'm just kidding. Hey, you're all right.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Uh, now children, if you have to answer nature's call during the night, use this bucket next to Bart's head.
Forget it. He releases the hounds on every charity that comes to his door: Feed the Children, Save the Whales, even Release the Hounds.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Uh, well, maybe we can pry open his wallet with a slick, professional pitch. A school play!
I don't know. What happened to the last Safety Salamander?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Uh... he fell asleep in the suit and suffocated.
Just call me "The Cleaner.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Um, where's the body?
That old gag.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Unfortunately, at the same moment, my mother was in the girls' lavatory making use of the facilities.
What cologne are you wearing? None of your business! Now we'd like our Washington Monument to be one five-hundredth the size of the real one.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Washington Monument? Aren't you gonna even try?
Pardon my galoshes.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Wasn't that wonderful? And now, "Santas of Many Lands," as presented by the entire second grade class.
Ooh, Papa John's.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: We will conclude by passing around a sheet on which I would like everyone's email address.
Well, what about Bart?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: We're looking. But in the meantime, the Class Clown Pro Tem will take his place.
Well, that's Bart for ya.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: We're talking about Lisa, your daughter.
There are no flights to London till five!

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Welcome to Springfield Elementary's Next Top Model... building contest.
What a week.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Welcome to another school year. One important note: the flower-based names of the reading groups are now barnyard-based. Mr. Becker has protested the move, so his group will remain the Daffodils.
We all went our separate ways.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well William, I'm back. So, how did you spend your summer?
Oh, no reason, really. I was just wondering if you know, you'd like to come over to my house for dinner. A payback for all the crummy things Bart has done to your school.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, a home-cooked meal would be a nice change of pace. I'd be delighted!
Wait a minute, Skinner. How do we know some principal over in France isn't pulling the same scam you are?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, for one thing, you wouldn't be getting a French boy. You would be getting an Albanian.
And Maggie, you no longer have to live with the burden of replacing Bart and Lisa.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, if this episode has taught us anything, it's that nothing works better than the status quo. Bart, you're promoted back to the fourth grade.
But if you weren't married to your job, you'd tend to go for a girl, right?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, of course. These pants come off at night just like everyone else's. But tell me, why all the questions?
Hear him out, Marge.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, perhaps I was being a tad glib. Let me explain. Our elementary school participates in a foreign exchange program. Now normally, a student is selected on the basis of academic excellence or intelligence, but in Bart's case I'm prepared to make a big exception. And, if you're willing to play along, he can spend the next three months studying far, far away.
Wow! And after them, out of all the people in the world, you chose me. Uh huh, yeah, number four and a half reed.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Well, you're in for a whale of a show tonight. I'd like to point out that the doors are now locked, so you parents can't sneak out of the show after your own child has performed. Oh, and let me caution the people in the first five rows, you will get wet.
Oh, okay.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: What a load of garbage! I'm ecstatic. With the money from this, we're within striking distance of our trip to Albany.
Is everyone here as sick of those stupid politicians as I am?

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: What about the media? They're not covering the issues, they just want to declare a frontrunner and go back to their mansions.
I'd like to return this barbecue kit.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: What's the matter, Edna? Lately you just say "Ha!" to everything.
Come on, it's your last night of freedom. You gotta have some fun.

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Who are all of you people?
Let's see where he's going with this...

dialogue.speaker: Seymour Skinner
dialogue.text: Willie! As your employer, I insist that you...
